title: The death of John the Baptist (29 August)
hook: the prophet dies for telling a king the truth

segments.voice: Yesterday, Joseph Calasanz, who taught children whose families couldn't pay. Your line was free schools.

The party is already loud. It's King Herod's birthday, and around his table sit his lords, his officers, the leading men of Galilee. Somewhere under his power sits a prisoner: a man who once wore camel hair by the Jordan, whom the king has locked up but can't bring himself to kill. Then a girl comes in and dances, and the king is so pleased that he makes a promise out loud, in front of everyone: ask me for whatever you want, up to half my kingdom. She goes out to ask her mother what to ask for.
screen: `A KING'S BIRTHDAY.` → `A PRISONER HE WON'T KILL.` → `A PROMISE IN FRONT OF EVERYONE.`

segments.voice: Mark tells it in his sixth chapter. Herod had married Herodias, his brother's wife, and John had said to him, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife." That's the whole offense. One sentence, and true. Herodias wanted him dead. Herod didn't, not quite. Mark gives a strange, honest detail: Herod feared John, "knowing him to be a just and holy man," and liked to listen to him. So the king kept the prophet locked up, and kept coming back to hear him. Then the dance, and the promise. The girl's mother tells her what to ask for: the head of John the Baptist. The girl hurries back and adds: on a dish. Mark says the king was struck with sorrow. But he had sworn, his guests were watching, and he couldn't stand to back down at his own party. So he sent the executioner. Afterward, John's disciples came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb. Notice who is free in this story. The king has the throne and the power, and he's trapped by an oath he made to look generous. The prisoner has nothing, and he's the one person in the room who said what was true. The Church calls this day the passion of John the Baptist, the same word it uses for the suffering of Christ. All his life John went ahead of Jesus, preparing the way. Catholics see him going ahead of Jesus here, too.
screen: `IT IS NOT LAWFUL FOR THEE.` · `HEROD FEARED HIM, AND LISTENED.` · `TRAPPED BY HIS OWN OATH.` · `GOING AHEAD, EVEN IN DEATH.` · then, large: `A JUST AND HOLY MAN.`

segments.voice: First, Herod's seat: notice something you keep up only because people are watching, a position, a promise, a story about yourself. Then John's place: bring to mind someone who may need a hard truth from you, and ask what they would need to know first, that you're on their side. If you pray, ask Saint John the Baptist for his courage; if not, just hold that person with goodwill.
Passion, the Church's word for John the Baptist's death: the prophet killed for telling King Herod the truth, kept on the twenty-ninth of August.
Your line: truth cost his head. In that room, the prisoner was the free one. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: On 29 August Catholics keep the Passion of Saint John the Baptist; the Gospel at Mass that day tells his death from the sixth chapter of Mark.

original.note: Greek: it is permitted, it is lawful. in Mark 6:18 John tells the king it is not: οὐκ ἔξεστιν.

chat.says: Why did John the Baptist get killed? What did he even do?
options: He told Herod his marriage to his brother's wife was unlawful; that cost him his life.
He insulted the king's guests at the birthday party and wouldn't apologize.
He broke the law by baptizing crowds without the Temple priests' permission.
chat.meaning: In Mark, John told Herod, "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife." One true sentence cost him his life.

Herod.meaning: the ruler who locked John up, yet feared him

Herodias.meaning: Herod's wife, once married to his brother

Galilee.meaning: the region whose leading men sat at Herod's table

Jordan.meaning: the river where John once preached and baptized

notes: The name Salome (from Josephus) is left out; Mark's manuscripts differ on how the girl is named (some read 'his daughter Herodias' at 6:22), so the script says only 'a girl'.
'Somewhere under his power sits a prisoner': Mark does not say where John was held (Josephus says Machaerus); kept vague on purpose.
'The Church calls this day the passion of John the Baptist': the Latin title is Passio S. Ioannis Baptistae. Confirm the English usage.
'Catholics see him going ahead of Jesus here, too': the forerunner-in-death theme is in the liturgy (e.g. Bede's homily read in the Office). Confirm phrasing.
Original: ἔξεστιν, Mark 6:18 οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι. Confirm.
Confirm Douay-Rheims wording of Mark 6:18 and 6:20.
